historical_references.reference: Kanaklata Devi was a legendary female warrior of the medieval period in Bengal, India. She is most famous for leading a band of women to defend her village against an invading army of Mughal soldiers, led by Raja Man Singh. The battle took place in 1650 in the village of Pratapgarh.

Another tale about Kanaklata Devi speaks of her leading a rebellion against the British East India Company in the late 19th century, during the Indian freedom struggle. She reportedly carried a trishula (a Hindu trident) and wore saffron robes, symbolizing her devotion to the Hindu goddess Kali.
